items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-12-09
items.q: he had, I was... He had a mile in order, you know, him and Johnny, uh, you know, Johnny Foster, Johnny Foster, I don't know, Walter Preston... And so they brought him to me... they were running over, you know, practicing

ctx.x: One thing I wanted to ask you about, which I did ask you about once before, but it was not, it was after the tape recorder gone out, is the time when, uh, the circumstances which led up to your playing with the E. Van Thomas Band. How did it come about that you went out there?

Oh, well, I did. Ruffin's, I remember mentioning that this, that this, poor man, poor man, not poor man, he's an ordinary poor, uh, Ruffins. I don't know what he meant with John, but every musician, you know, you would book dances. I was a musician, uh, Lafayette and Lafayette and Lafayette, and I'm up to Lafayette. Well, I went up with Chris Kelly, uh, and, uh, they had a battle in Lafayette. We had Thomas and Chris Kelly. Well, he vagued. I'll play Chris in the one set because he was a better musician than the…
But you had started a job when you, when he was killed. I mean, you had been paying for a job.
